title: No Surprises Act (IDR) Medical Arbitration & Out-of-Network Recovery — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: Field worksheets for screening protected claims, routing disputes to the right forum, verifying the QPA, filing federal IDR on time, and pricing every offer against the rulebook and the IDR scoreboard

worksheets.title: Protected-Claim Screen and Balance-Billing Exposure Map
worksheets.purpose: Sort every surprise bill into the protected lanes of emergency care, air ambulance, and non-emergency care at in-network facilities, separate the excluded ground ambulance and non-hospital claims, and hold the patient to in-network cost sharing while every disputed dollar moves into the right escalation path.
instructions: Freeze every payment, payment plan, and card charge on the account before working any field, because a payment plan can be read as acceptance of the full amount.
Classify the claim into a protected lane or the excluded column first, since ground ambulance, urgent care, and non-hospital facilities sit outside the ban.
Get written confirmation of plan funding from HR before relying on any state surprise billing law, because state protections stop at self-funded plans.
Cite the exact source, timestamp, and dollar figure behind each entry so every complaint, appeal, or reprocessing request can be defended line by line.
Load every appeal, dispute, and negotiation clock into one tracker on the day the triggering bill or denial arrives, never after the fact.

fields.name: lane_classification
fields.prompt: Classify the claim into one of the three protected lanes: emergency care, air ambulance, or non-emergency care at an in-network facility. Record the facility network status, the service date, and the reason the claim does or does not fall inside the ban.
fields.example: In-network-facility lane: an appendectomy at an in-network hospital with an out-of-network surgeon, anesthesiologist, and radiologist billed $14,238, and a No Surprises Help Desk complaint wiped $9,800 within 6 weeks [Bill Fighter — OWN7CBskcIQ @ 00:09:41]. Ground ambulance is excluded, because the helicopter is protected and the road is not [AS DESIGNED | Risk & Insurance Stories — w_lpas-cNkc @ 00:06:05].

fields.name: waiver_check
fields.prompt: List every provider on the claim and flag hospital-based ancillary specialties such as anesthesiology, radiology, pathology, emergency medicine, neonatology, and hospitalists. Note whether any notice-and-consent document was signed, who signed it, and whether that specialty could ever lawfully waive protections.
fields.example: Anesthesiology group consent form found in the chart: flagged as unenforceable, because emergency medicine, anesthesiology, pathology, radiology, neonatology, hospitalists, diagnostics, and air ambulance can never be waived [CMSHHSgov — aQ87InetyaA @ 00:27:28]. Copy retained for 7 years, noting consent is very difficult to obtain [Holland & Hart LLP — aaDjROGKKC0 @ 00:39:06]. Member billed at in-network cost sharing only.

fields.name: plan_funding_status
fields.prompt: Record whether the plan is fully insured or self-funded, the written source of that answer, and whether any state surprise billing law can reach the claim. Note the HR contact, the plan document section relied on, and any card markings.
fields.example: HR confirmed in writing, citing the plan document rather than the brochure, that the plan is self-funded, so the state ground ambulance law reaching only fully insured plans does not apply [AS DESIGNED | Risk & Insurance Stories — w_lpas-cNkc @ 00:15:10]. The member card showed only a small 'sf', so the written answer controlled [Miller Johnson — EwlPyAVGU8k @ 00:08:21].

fields.name: cost_sharing_check
fields.prompt: Compare the patient's billed responsibility against in-network cost sharing. Record billed charges, allowed amount, deductible applied, coinsurance, and any balance billed above that amount. Flag every dollar charged to the patient beyond in-network cost sharing as a potential violation for complaint.
fields.example: Self-funded Arizona plan, anesthesiology group: billed $42,000, QPA roughly $18,000, final allowed just over $21,000 after IDR sided with the plan, about $20,000 saved, and no balance bill to the member [Jentry Harris — LNSPlo2_U3c @ 00:02:13]. Member responsibility recorded at in-network cost sharing only, with the excess logged as a plan-to-provider payment dispute, not patient debt.

fields.name: itemized_bill_audit
fields.prompt: Request the itemized bill with CPT codes and write down each disputed line with its reason before paying anything. Record duplicate charges, mismatched codes, and services not received, and note that auditors find errors in up to 80% of bills.
fields.example: Payments, payment plan, and card charge frozen until the itemized bill was reviewed and every disputed line written down with its reason [Problem Solved Lab — ofqIwNzp8lA @ 00:03:31]. No payment plan signed, because a payment plan can be read as acceptance of the full amount [Problem Solved Lab — ofqIwNzp8lA @ 00:03:46]. Disputed lines routed to the insurer for reprocessing.

fields.name: emergency_status
fields.prompt: Document why the visit qualifies as emergency care under the prudent layperson standard. Record the symptoms as the patient experienced them, the denial reason the plan gave, and the date the 120-day appeal clock started running.
fields.example: ER claim denied as non-emergency; appeal framed on the prudent layperson standard, meaning a reasonable person in the patient's situation would have gone to the ER [Evolutio Labs — HwCCcS3hQls @ 00:01:03]. The 120-day appeal clock was calendared from the denial date the day the letter arrived [Evolutio Labs — HwCCcS3hQls @ 00:02:12]. The insurer was called first.

fields.name: lab_and_network_question
fields.prompt: Before ancillary work such as blood draws, record which lab receives the samples and whether it is in network. Capture the exact question asked of staff, the answer given, and the fallback plan if network status cannot be confirmed.
fields.example: Checkout staff asked which lab gets the samples; they could not confirm network status, so the lab prescription was requested and taken to an in-network lab [Insured and Informed — wySlaLru-l4 @ 00:03:36]. Question logged as 'Am I in network?', never 'Do you accept my insurance?' [FOX 26 Houston — 9dOW3txIHG0 @ 00:02:07]. Lab status flagged as contested among practitioners.

fields.name: complaint_escalation
fields.prompt: Map the escalation path for an improper bill: insurer reprocessing call, collection agency script, and No Surprises Help Desk complaint at 1-800-985-3059. Record each contact date, representative, reference number, and the outcome promised at every step.
fields.example: Step one: insurer asked to reprocess as an in-network claim. Step two: collection agency told the bill appears to violate the No Surprises Act and asked to stop collection and reprocess through insurance [Share My Lesson — Q11eG-8d-Hw @ 00:04:22]. Step three: Help Desk complaint at 1-800-985-3059, the route that erased $9,800 of a $14,238 bill [Bill Fighter — OWN7CBskcIQ @ 00:09:41].

fields.name: uninsured_dispute
fields.prompt: For self-pay or uninsured patients, compare the final bill to the written good faith estimate. Record the estimate amount, billed amount, difference per provider, date of the first bill, and whether the $25 dispute can still be filed.
fields.example: Self-pay patient kept the written estimate: $300 estimated against an $850 bill, which clears the $400-over threshold per provider [CMSHHSgov — RRI2VT8QiiI @ 00:40:00]. Dispute filed with the $25 fee inside 120 days from the first bill [Law Unpacked — 0NouMpFWLHI @ 00:02:32]. Collections and late-fee accrual suspended while the case is pending [DAS Health — e5b1ICVPSZs @ 00:42:00].

fields.name: deadline_tracker
fields.prompt: Load every open-negotiation, initiation, and offer deadline into one tracker before the first dispute. Record the trigger date for each clock, the computed due date, the owner responsible, and the confirmation that each step was completed on time.
fields.example: Tracker built before the first filing: 30-business-day open negotiation, then the initiation window, then offer dates, because missing a deadline by a day or two can invalidate the IDR [PYA, PC — j1DGgPw1__E @ 00:26:37]. Every final offer priced against winner-takes-all selection, since the arbitrator picks one offer and not the average [Jentry Harris — LNSPlo2_U3c @ 00:01:29].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not advance until every claim sits in a protected lane or the excluded column, plan funding is confirmed in writing, every ancillary waiver is flagged as unenforceable, all payments are frozen pending the itemized audit, and every appeal, dispute, and negotiation deadline is loaded into one tracker with a named owner.

worksheets.title: Forum Routing, QPA Verification, and Federal IDR Initiation
worksheets.purpose: Route each out-of-network claim to the one process that governs it, test the plan's QPA against its required methodology and disclosures, pass the three-part eligibility screen, and move from a documented open negotiation into a timely, fully paid federal IDR initiation without losing the claim to a missed window.
instructions: Confirm plan funding and the state route before touching the federal portal, because a claim sent to the wrong process gets kicked out.
Read the remittance for a QPA before choosing a forum, since a plan sends the QPA when it believes federal law applies.
Present the full case during open negotiation, because new information is not supposed to be added once the dispute reaches arbitration.
Assemble the entire IDR submission offline before opening the portal, since the form times out at 50 minutes and windows run in days.
Pay both the certified IDR entity fee and the administrative fee with the offer, or the other side's offer wins by default.

fields.name: forum_precedence
fields.prompt: Determine which dispute process governs the claim using the precedence of all-payer model, specified state law, then federal IDR. Record plan funding, state of service, any opt-in by a self-funded ERISA plan, and why only one process applies.
fields.example: Self-funded ERISA plan with no state opt-in: routed to federal IDR, following all-payer model, specified state law, then federal precedence. Logged with the AMA position that there should be one process for any given claim, either the state or the federal process [American Medical Association (AMA) — 6_ODgJ97UtA @ 00:54:45]. Misrouted claims get kicked out [Ryan Downs — 7lqb5ev54mA @ 00:01:25].

fields.name: qpa_on_remit
fields.prompt: Read the remittance advice and record whether the plan sent a QPA with it, the QPA amount, the CPT code, and the billed charge. Note whether the QPA signal indicates the plan believes federal law applies to this claim.
fields.example: Remittance arrived with a QPA attached, which signals the plan believes federal law applies [American Medical Association (AMA) — 6_ODgJ97UtA @ 00:19:50]. Out-of-network MRI, CPT 72148: $4,800 billed against a QPA of about $1,200 [AHealthcareZ - Healthcare Finance Explained — NFJaCM_6M_Y @ 00:07:28]. QPA logged as the basis for cost sharing, not a minimum payment.

fields.name: qpa_disclosure_request
fields.prompt: Draft the on-demand QPA disclosure request. List each element requested, including non-fee-for-service rate use, the eligible database used, related codes, and excluded incentive payments, plus the date sent, the plan contact, and the response received.
fields.example: Request sent for non-fee-for-service rate use, the database used, related codes, and excluded incentive payments, which the plan must supply on request [CMSHHSgov — Sp7aK2UsmlE @ 00:36:07]. QPA checked against its build: 2019 median contracted rate, at least 3 rates, indexed for inflation. Carrier databases noted as unverified, a black box [Becker's Hospital Review — RJps0omOazk @ 00:53:01].

fields.name: qpa_methodology_exposure
fields.prompt: Test the plan's QPA math for compliance issues. Record whether each contract rate was counted once regardless of claim volume, who paid for the eligible database, and any penalty exposure the plan faces for a faulty methodology.
fields.example: Suspected per-claim rate counting flagged, because a rate negotiated under a contract constitutes a single contracted rate regardless of claims paid at it [CMSHHSgov — Sp7aK2UsmlE @ 00:10:58]. Database cost belongs to the plan [CMSHHSgov — Sp7aK2UsmlE @ 00:31:54]. Exposure noted: up to $100 per day, per entity, per affected individual [CMSHHSgov — Sp7aK2UsmlE @ 00:48:11].

fields.name: eligibility_three_doors
fields.prompt: Run the three-part eligibility test before filing. Record which door the claim enters: ED-admitted out-of-network event, out-of-network clinician on an in-network event, or emergency air ambulance. Note any waived protections, Medicare or Medicaid coverage, or contracted status.
fields.example: Door two: out-of-network clinician on an in-network event. Anesthesia checked as elective, eligible only because the facility was in-network [The Phia Group, LLC — ksxW878eWWk @ 00:06:46]. Consent waiver absent, since waived protections make a dispute ineligible [CMSHHSgov — cw4MI_h6Gns @ 00:05:03]. Screen matters: one in five disputes is thrown out as ineligible [Staffingly, Inc — ASHyX7v13Eo @ 00:01:25].

fields.name: open_negotiation_record
fields.prompt: Log the open negotiation. Record the initial payment or denial date, the date negotiation was invoked within 30 business days, the counteroffers exchanged, and the full case presented, since new information should not be added at arbitration.
fields.example: Open negotiation invoked within 30 business days of the initial payment, with proof of the start date uploaded, since initiations lacking it are held [CMSHHSgov — cw4MI_h6Gns @ 00:04:22]. Full case presented to the plan up front, because by arbitration you are not supposed to add information [Miller Johnson — EwlPyAVGU8k @ 00:27:15]. Every good-faith outreach logged for submission.

fields.name: initiation_window
fields.prompt: Calculate the initiation deadline. Record the last day of open negotiation, the four-business-day filing window that follows, the date the submission was assembled offline, and the date it was filed on the federal portal with its confirmation number.
fields.example: Negotiation failed on business day 30; four business days counted forward to the initiation deadline [Ryan Downs — 7lqb5ev54mA @ 00:05:15]. Full submission assembled offline before opening the portal, because the form times out at 50 minutes [American Medical Association (AMA) — 6_ODgJ97UtA @ 00:24:00]. Staffingly calls the four-day window absolute, so filing was scheduled ahead of the last day.

fields.name: idre_selection
fields.prompt: Record the certified IDR entity selection. Note entities used before and whether to reject one, what each entity treats as a successful argument, and whether the parties agreed or the federal government picked the entity for this dispute.
fields.example: Previously used entity rejected, which is permitted, and payer down-coding challenged in the same filing [PYA, PC — j1DGgPw1__E @ 00:55:18]. Feedback gathered by meeting entities and asking what they treat as a successful argument, then folded into the submission [Ryan Downs — 7lqb5ev54mA @ 00:09:44]. No agreement within the window means the federal government picks one.

fields.name: fee_and_offer
fields.prompt: Confirm that both the certified IDR entity fee and the administrative fee were paid together with the offer. Record amounts, payment dates, the offer figure, and the evidence supporting it, including prior in-network rates and down-coding explanations.
fields.example: Entity fee and administrative fee paid with the offer, because an offer is not received until both are paid, and an unreceived offer hands the other side its number [CMSHHSgov — 7lzQt8aAlG0 @ 00:25:17]. Offer supported by the provider's prior in-network rates from the past 4 years [PYA, PC — j1DGgPw1__E @ 00:30:31]. Plan required to explain any down-coding.

fields.name: target_inventory
fields.prompt: Rank the underpaid out-of-network inventory by net recoverable value. Record payment as a percentage of billed charges, likely additional payment, filing expense, specialist effort, days remaining on the clock, and aggregate variance across recurring claims.
fields.example: Target band: claims paid 15 to 17% of charges, pushed toward 45 to 55% [Ryan Downs — 7lqb5ev54mA @ 00:03:38]. Ranked by likely additional payment, filing expense, specialist effort, and time remaining [Vee Healthtek — s3194z7bdwY @ 00:00:54]. Small variances aggregated: a $200 gap across 5,000 claims equals $1 million before fees [Vee Healthtek — GpHExH5dquQ @ 00:01:25].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not file until the governing forum is documented, the QPA is read from the remittance and its disclosures requested, the claim passes one eligibility door with no waiver, proof of the open negotiation start date is uploaded, the four-business-day deadline is calendared, and both fees are paid with the offer.

worksheets.title: Rule-Change Compliance and IDR Scoreboard Economics
worksheets.purpose: Keep every dispute compliant with the operations final rule on batching, fees, response deadlines, cooling-off periods, and plan registration, then price each claim and entity choice against the IDR scoreboard so that only viable disputes are filed and every award is tracked until cash actually lands.
instructions: Split the caseload by open-negotiation start date relative to November 1, 2026 before applying any batching or deadline rule.
Verify the current administrative and entity fees before every payment, because paying the wrong fee means the offer is denied.
Hard-calendar the four-business-day filing window after the 30-business-day cooling-off period, since the portal allows no grace period.
Price every claim against the full fee load and realistic recovery share before filing, regardless of how strong the headline win rates look.
Track every award against the 30-calendar-day payment deadline and never book an award as cash until the funds actually arrive.

fields.name: rule_change_split
fields.prompt: Split the caseload by open-negotiation start date relative to November 1, 2026. Record which disputes follow prior single, bundled, and batch rules, which fall under the 50-line-item cap, and the calendar tool tracking each group.
fields.example: Two tracking systems keyed on open-negotiation start date, run on a calendar-based tool rather than spreadsheets [Xpert Billing Talk — g3C-DoM_9CI @ 00:01:47]. Post-November 1, 2026 batches capped at exactly 50 line items; older disputes keep prior rules [Xpert Billing Talk — g3C-DoM_9CI @ 00:00:45]. Batch-cap baseline flagged as disputed: 25 or unlimited.

fields.name: batch_code_check
fields.prompt: Review every line item grouped for batching. Record the Category I CPT codes, eligibility of each code, whether any ineligible code is mixed in, and the coder who cross-referenced the batch manually before submission to the federal portal.
fields.example: Radiology batch cross-referenced manually on Category I CPT codes, because mixing eligible and ineligible codes triggers automatic rejection [Xpert Billing Talk — g3C-DoM_9CI @ 00:03:22]. Initiating party confirmed every resubmitted line meets batching and bundling criteria [CMSHHSgov — Vy31vkzfNBE @ 00:04:24]. New Hampshire state route noted separately: up to 25 items per single fee [New Hampshire Insurance Department — C6hIoQuEWeA @ 00:04:45].

fields.name: fee_verification
fields.prompt: Verify the current administrative and entity fees before every payment. Record the fee schedule date checked, the amount paid per party, the effective date of any change, and confirmation that the offer was accepted as received.
fields.example: Administrative fee confirmed at $15 per party, $30 total, cut from $115 effective June 11, 2026 [HaloMD — of6CD7esHY0 @ 00:02:33]. Checked before each payment, because paying the wrong fee means the offer is denied [The Phia Group, LLC — ksxW878eWWk @ 00:17:28]. Lower fee logged as a likely driver of another filing surge.

fields.name: cooling_off_and_response
fields.prompt: Calendar the response and filing dates under the operations final rule. Record the business-day-15 response deadline for the non-initiating party, the 30-business-day cooling-off end date, and the four-business-day filing window with no grace period.
fields.example: Payer response due by business day 15 of open negotiation [KLGatesLaw — NwapzBNojY0 @ 00:04:19]. Filing window hard-calendared after the 30-business-day cooling-off period, since the portal blocks late filings with no grace period and dumps them into denial queues as permanent losses [Xpert Billing Talk — g3C-DoM_9CI @ 00:02:36]. Change flagged: do not miss it or cases expire.

fields.name: plan_registration
fields.prompt: For plan-side operators, confirm the plan is registered in the IDR registry before the deadline. Record the registration date, the steps covered going forward, outstanding disputes at risk of default, and the good-faith outreach log.
fields.example: Plan registered ahead of the deadline, because an unregistered plan cannot respond, defaults at the offer stage, and late registration only covers steps going forward [HaloMD — of6CD7esHY0 @ 00:19:47]. Every good-faith outreach to billing agencies logged and submitted in IDR, where it is considered, unlike litigation settlement talks [The Phia Group, LLC — ksxW878eWWk @ 00:03:31].

fields.name: award_payment_tracker
fields.prompt: Track every award against the 30-calendar-day payment deadline. Record the determination date, prevailing offer, amount due, date paid, and any shortfall, and do not book an award as cash until the funds actually land.
fields.example: Award tracker run against the 30-calendar-day deadline, since unpaid awards carry reputational and regulatory risk without a private right of action [The Phia Group, LLC — ksxW878eWWk @ 00:14:13]. Awards booked only when cash lands: about 30% of HaloMD's 400,000 awards were unpaid, Anthem at 74% [Long Reads, Explained — nJ5Tz7G_LA8 @ 00:04:46].

fields.name: scoreboard_benchmarks
fields.prompt: Record the scoreboard benchmarks used to set offer expectations. Capture the provider win rate, average award relative to QPA, dispute volume against the original projection, and the source and period for each figure cited in planning.
fields.example: Providers won 85% of 2024 disputes at an average award of 445% of QPA [Zelis Healthcare — lhoUoQSpOCg @ 00:01:25]. Volume: 2.6 million provider disputes in 2025 against roughly 17,000 expected per year [Long Reads, Explained — cSaC2n-3r9o @ 00:06:58]. Total 2025 awards reached $14.85B, over three times 2024's $4.08B [Top Hospitals USA — eDCqqjk5fqk @ 00:00:00].

fields.name: claim_viability_pricing
fields.prompt: Price the claim against the fee load before filing. Record the charge, the QPA, the gap between them, the expected share of that gap recovered, the total per-dispute cost, and the win rate needed to break even.
fields.example: Radiology claim priced first: recovering one quarter of the charge-minus-QPA gap leaves only 11 to 22% of radiology claims viable [AJR Radiology — rYqWvbw_kGo @ 00:04:54]. Unit QPA of $50 against $1,000 per dispute means a 50 to 60% win rate loses money [About The Rest — WdSfoeegaaI @ 00:20:44]. Low-value units held back from filing.

fields.name: idre_ranking
fields.prompt: Rank IDR entities on operational performance. Record refund speed, eligibility accuracy, ACH refund enrollment status, verbal bank authentication requirements, and custom report availability for each entity, then note win ratio last as the final tiebreaker.
fields.example: Good entities refund in 5 days against a 30-business-day allowance, so refund speed and eligibility accuracy rank ahead of win ratio [HaloMD — g2udecJ21bI @ 00:28:04]. ACH refunds enrolled with all 11 entities, including those requiring verbal bank authentication, with weekly custom reports from the 6 entities that offer them [HaloMD — g2udecJ21bI @ 00:21:09].

fields.name: plan_side_exposure
fields.prompt: For employer and plan sponsors, measure IDR exposure. Record whether claims data flags IDR claims, the carrier's response to that request, hidden reversals repaid higher, and the share of medical spend going to IDR this plan year.
fields.example: Claims data requested with IDR claims flagged; not knowing which claims went through IDR is almost de facto inadequate fiduciary conduct [AHealthcareZ - Healthcare Finance Explained — 6E_HRECi-t8 @ 00:07:50]. Hidden claims hunted by flagging payments reversed 2 to 6 months later and repaid much higher [Payerset — lqE3aZxq024 @ 00:39:40]. Benchmark: one employer reports 24% of medical claims spend on IDR.

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not file or pay until every dispute is assigned to the pre- or post-November 1 system, each batch is code-checked, current fees are verified, response and filing windows are hard-calendared, the claim clears the fee-load viability test, and every open award sits on the payment tracker as receivable, not cash.

worksheets.title: Winning vs. Getting Paid: Award Collection and Out-of-Network Facility Recovery
worksheets.purpose: Turn won IDR awards into deposited cash and protect out-of-network facility revenue. Price each dispute before filing, screen eligibility up front, and escalate unpaid awards in bulk. Defend negotiated allowances, single case agreements, and EOB adjustments against recoupment, voided agreements, and silent PPO layering.
instructions: Pull every IDR award and out-of-network facility claim from the last twelve months before writing a single answer.
Treat an award as cash only after funds land in the bank, and record unpaid awards in a separate pending bucket.
Price each dispute type against the full per-dispute cost before deciding whether IDR, negotiation, or the threat of IDR is the right tool.
Attach the signed award letter, negotiation form, or EOB to every field answer that cites a dollar figure.
Assign one named owner and a calendared deadline to each unpaid award and each open out-of-network appeal.

fields.name: award_cash_status_ledger
fields.prompt: List every IDR award your group has won in the last twelve months, the payer, the award date, the amount, and whether cash has actually landed. Mark each award as paid, partially paid, or unpaid, and note the days elapsed since determination.
fields.example: Anthem awards: 14 won, 4 paid, 10 unpaid past 30 calendar days. We stopped booking awards as cash after reading that about 30 percent of HaloMD's 400,000 awards were unpaid, with Anthem at 74 percent [Long Reads, Explained — nJ5Tz7G_LA8 @ 00:04:46]. Unpaid Anthem awards now sit in a separate pending-collection bucket, not in recognized revenue.

fields.name: pre_filing_dispute_economics
fields.prompt: For each specialty line you plan to file, compare the expected QPA per unit or claim against the full per-dispute cost, then estimate the win rate you need to break even. Flag any claim type where a coin-flip win rate loses money.
fields.example: Anesthesia low-unit claims: QPA near $50 a unit against roughly $1,000 per dispute, so a 50 to 60 percent win rate loses money [About The Rest — WdSfoeegaaI @ 00:20:44]. We moved those claims out of the IDR queue and into pre-filing negotiation, using the threat of IDR itself as leverage [About The Rest — WdSfoeegaaI @ 00:26:55].

fields.name: eligibility_refusal_screen
fields.prompt: Name the eligibility grounds insurers most often use to refuse payment on your won awards, and describe the up-front screen you will run before filing so those same grounds cannot be raised after the determination is issued.
fields.example: Our pre-filing screen checks four refusal grounds: missed deadlines, Medicare beneficiaries, Medicaid beneficiaries, and providers that were actually contracted with the plan [Long Reads, Explained — nJ5Tz7G_LA8 @ 00:08:37]. Any claim failing one check is pulled before filing. Last quarter that screen removed 31 claims that would have produced awards the payer could refuse to honor.

fields.name: collection_escalation_path
fields.prompt: Map your escalation path for an award still unpaid after the payment deadline: AR follow-up steps, the documents attached to each contact, when you file regulator complaints, and whether a contingency recovery service enters. Note who owns each step.
fields.example: Step one: AR call with the signed award letter attached. Step two: bulk complaints to state departments of insurance, treated as pre-litigation rather than single CMS tickets [Apex IONM Solutions — gbhlBlDLViQ @ 00:05:45]. Step three: awards unpaid near two years go to a contingency shop charging 8 percent of the amount recovered, payable after funds arrive [CollectionPro Services LLC — Ahr00pn-Tiw @ 00:01:16].

fields.name: enforcement_leverage_notes
fields.prompt: Describe the leverage you hold when no private right of action exists and federal fines have not been issued. Include employer-facing pressure, regulatory complaints, and policy advocacy, and state which lever you will pull first against your worst-paying payer.
fields.example: A provider group cannot technically sue for unpaid arbitrated awards [Apex IONM Solutions — gbhlBlDLViQ @ 00:02:00], and no penalty has been issued [Long Reads, Explained — nJ5Tz7G_LA8 @ 00:12:00]. Our first lever is the employer angle: Elevance disclosed to employers that it withholds award payments, creating ERISA exposure for those plans [TopMedTalk — 0BcGdvWG_UI @ 00:13:07].

fields.name: market_rate_evidence_pull
fields.prompt: Record the transparency data you will pull to prove market value before filing: plan, zip code, CPT, and TIN. State the market rate you found as a percentage of Medicare and compare it with what the plan actually paid.
fields.example: TIN lookup on the anesthesia group: transparency allowed-amount data filtered by plan, zip, CPT, and TIN showed a market rate near 250 percent of Medicare, while the plan paid 120 percent [The Doctors Lounge — QITUqT322Iw @ 00:41:15]. That gap becomes the opening exhibit, set against plans losing 85 to 90 percent of cases [The Doctors Lounge — QITUqT322Iw @ 00:38:48].

fields.name: oon_benefit_verification_log
fields.prompt: For each out-of-network facility case, record when benefits were verified, the allowance methodology and pricer identified, whether the plan pays on UCR, and whether the employer SPD was obtained. Note how many hours elapsed between scheduling and verification.
fields.example: ASC case 2291: benefits verified within 24 hours, UCR plan confirmed, SPD pulled from the employer. UCR plans go to the front of the line, since two UCR claims at 60 to 70 percent of charges equal roughly 30 in-network claims [Patriot Group — dUdxVBDLf5w @ 00:08:25]. Follow-up is set at 10 days, not 20.

fields.name: negotiation_and_settlement_record
fields.prompt: Document every pre-payment or post-payment negotiation: first offer received, counteroffer made, final agreed number, and the channel used. Explain how the signed form proves the agreed amount and why you did or did not accept a portal settlement offer.
fields.example: Repricer opened at 62 percent of charges; we countered, since the rule is never accept the first negotiation offer [Plano Texas — w387XkK0lkk @ 00:09:47], and wrote 'max allowable' on the signed form [Plano Texas — w387XkK0lkk @ 00:28:40]. We refused the portal offer because portals allow only accept or decline [Becker's Hospital Review — 7h4H8g1S01E @ 00:24:23].

fields.name: single_case_agreement_defense
fields.prompt: For every single case agreement you rely on, record the documented proof that no in-network facility exists within 50 miles, the EOB date that starts the out-of-network appeal clock, and the calendared deadline for filing that appeal.
fields.example: SCA with UMR, approved, then voided after payment. Our file holds call notes from three competitor facilities confirming none are in network within 50 miles. The EOB is dated March 3, so the appeal deadline is exactly 180 days out, versus 365 in-network [AR Specialist — OLFRzRe0L2A @ 00:06:34]. Manual review is budgeted at about 30 days.

fields.name: eob_layering_and_clawback_audit
fields.prompt: Before posting any adjustment, audit the EOB for stacked repricing networks and confirm the patient file holds the out-of-network disclosure, financial agreement, and cost-share letter. Record what you found and what you corrected before the adjustment was posted.
fields.example: EOB showed two silent PPO discounts layered on one claim, capping the allowable near 35 percent [Collect Rx — Pqx2hpp_cLU @ 00:18:50]; we held posting and appealed. The file had the disclosure and financial agreement but no cost-share letter, so we sent one, avoiding the fee-forgiveness clawback risk seen in Cigna exposure in the millions [Patriot Group — dUdxVBDLf5w @ 00:11:30].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not advance to Worksheet 5 until every won award is labeled paid, partially paid, or unpaid; every dispute line has a break-even win rate; every single case agreement carries documented 50-mile proof and a calendared 180-day appeal date; and every unpaid award has a named escalation owner.

worksheets.title: Superbills, Out-of-Network Benefits, and the Revenue Cycle Engine
worksheets.purpose: Build a clean two-track cash practice model in which superbills or courtesy billing reimburse patients without rejections. Then harden the front-, mid-, and back-end revenue cycle so that registration errors, stalled AR, and silent charge-offs stop draining collections before anyone notices.
instructions: Collect one recent superbill, one courtesy-billed claim, and last month's AR aging report before starting.
Use real per-CPT charges and real allowed amounts, and never substitute estimates where a remittance already exists.
Write the benefit-quoting policy as a rule that front desk staff can repeat word for word.
Confirm payment posting is current to the deposit date before answering any AR follow-up field.
Report gross charges, net revenue, and cash as three separate numbers in every field that asks about revenue.

fields.name: superbill_required_elements
fields.prompt: Audit one recent superbill line by line and list every required element it carries: provider name and credentials, individual NPI, license number, tax ID, CPT, place of service, diagnosis code, fee, and amount paid. Note any missing field.
fields.example: Superbill for client 0417 carried name, credentials, EIN, CPT code, diagnosis, fee, and amount paid, but no individual NPI and no place-of-service code. A missing field is what bounces submissions [Craft Your Practice — tkUfu8WA56U @ 00:05:12]. We added both to the template, and the client's resubmission was accepted on the next cycle without further requests.

fields.name: fee_schedule_and_package_pricing
fields.prompt: Write out your per-CPT fee schedule and confirm each charge is identical for every patient and session length. Explain how package pricing and full-hour pricing appear as line-item discounts that match exactly what the patient actually paid.
fields.example: One evaluation code and one treatment code, each billed at the same charge for every patient. A ten-visit package appears as full charges with a line-item discount equal to the package savings, so the superbill matches cash paid [Jarod Carter — heiuukmxgss @ 00:07:34]. Packages under four figures are collected in full, not split into payments [Jarod Carter — cA7tBJf4KyY @ 00:10:57].

fields.name: claim_track_choice
fields.prompt: State whether each payer lane runs on patient self-submitted superbills or courtesy billing with assignment declined. Explain how you confirm the accept-assignment box stays unchecked and the remit-payment box stays blank so reimbursement goes to the client.
fields.example: Two payers are courtesy billed; everyone else gets a monthly superbill. On courtesy claims, accept assignment is left unchecked and the remit-payment box blank [Alicia Murray | The Therapist HQ 🪩 — eXrZnEwRRH4 @ 00:09:00], because selecting no on accept assignment sends the money to the client [Kym Tolson The Traveling Therapist — FpNL1YIlvD0 @ 00:02:12].

fields.name: patient_responsibility_math
fields.prompt: Work one real out-of-network example from charge to patient balance: the fee, the allowed amount, the separate out-of-network deductible status, coinsurance percentage, coinsurance dollars, and any balance bill. Show the arithmetic so the patient can follow every step.
fields.example: Charge $250 for the hour; out-of-network allowed amount $100; deductible met; coinsurance 35 percent equals $35; balance bill $150 because assignment was not accepted; patient owes $185 total [The Private Practice Outsider — TNKYk9V0ty8 @ 00:01:58]. The allowed amount combines the benefit plan and the fee schedule, so it is not the fee schedule itself [Inlera University — 3JOMCnMqhvI @ 00:01:27].

fields.name: benefit_quoting_policy
fields.prompt: Decide whether your practice will quote out-of-network benefits to patients or route them to a self-service checker. Record the policy, the tool if any, its monthly cost, and how you handle blame when a claim later denies.
fields.example: Staff no longer quote benefits, since the practice gets blamed when claims deny. Instead, the fees page embeds the Mentaya checker at $29 a month after a free month, with a schedule-now button underneath [Alicia Murray | The Therapist HQ 🪩 — eXrZnEwRRH4 @ 00:23:09]. Patients see their own estimate, and the intake form records that the estimate came from their plan.

fields.name: payer_identification_and_submission_cadence
fields.prompt: Record the identifiers you give payers on every out-of-network call, the order you give them, and how often superbills are issued. Note the shortest member submission window among your payers and how your cadence stays inside it.
fields.example: NPI first, then EIN, because payers never locate an out-of-network provider by tax ID but find the NPI right away [Dr. Lauren Baker — zsaby8gJNmg @ 00:13:48]. One plan caps member submissions at ninety days, so superbills go out monthly through the software instead of letting clients hoard six months of paperwork [Craft Your Practice — tkUfu8WA56U @ 00:09:32].

fields.name: contract_drop_test
fields.prompt: Before dropping any payer contract, compare what that payer pays on full out-of-network charges with your self-pay rate. Record both numbers per visit, the payer names, and your decision on whether going out of network raises net revenue.
fields.example: Benchmark case: a coaching client with a self-pay rate near $179 sends full charges to two popular payers and collects about $220 a visit [Jarod Carter — cA7tBJf4KyY @ 00:06:06]. Our own test showed one payer at $205 out of network against our $170 self-pay rate, so that contract was dropped and full charges now go out.

fields.name: front_end_denial_prevention
fields.prompt: Describe your registration and financial-clearance checks, including when eligibility is verified, who confirms demographic details, and how fast clean claims drop. Name one front-end error that produced a denial in the last quarter and the control added afterward.
fields.example: Eligibility is verified the night before, claims are scrubbed per payer and dropped within 24 to 48 hours. Last quarter a missed middle initial produced a hard denial 30 days later, matching the warning that over 80 percent of denials start in registration [RCMOpsPro — RddJn-tA3OM @ 00:00:40]. Front desk now reads the name back against the card.

fields.name: ar_follow_up_rules
fields.prompt: Write your AR follow-up rules: posting status required before calls begin, minimum claim age before a call, daily account targets per specialist, payer buckets used, and how notes are left so the next caller never repeats research.
fields.example: No calls until posting is current to the bank-deposit date and reconciled with the bookkeeper [Inlera University — RvLjKE1S1eU @ 00:25:58]. Claims under three weeks old are skipped; each specialist works 40 to 60 accounts daily. Medicare Advantage sits in its own bucket, since its share of AR over 90 days rose from 19 to 36 percent [PayerWatch — cePrn8Rhav8 @ 00:49:55].

fields.name: revenue_reporting_and_zero_pay_triage
fields.prompt: Explain how you report gross charges, net revenue, and cash separately each month, and how you triage zero-pay claims by reason code. Include the monthly AR check against expected volume that would expose silent charge-offs or payer-matrix shortcuts.
fields.example: Gross, net, and cash run as three separate lines, because a payer-mix shift can send gross off the charts while net plummets [PayerWatch — cePrn8Rhav8 @ 00:26:11]. Zero-pays are sorted into deductible, out-of-network, maxed benefits, and termed policy; termed policies trigger a patient call and updates to both PM and EHR [Amazing Charts — eKRUeJa5ZzQ @ 00:25:53].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not advance to Worksheet 6 until the superbill template carries every required element, per-CPT charges are identical across patients, the claim track for each payer is written down, posting is current to the deposit date, and gross, net, and cash are reported as separate numbers.

worksheets.title: Decoding Remittances and Scaling Back-End Recovery
worksheets.purpose: Read every remittance down to group codes, CARCs, and RARCs, and reconcile each batch to the bank deposit. Expose contract underpayments and recurring denial causes. Build a financial case for automation and vendor controls in which humans still sign exceptions and control the release of held claims.
instructions: Export the last ten 835 files and the matching bank deposits before answering any field.
Open raw 835 files only in a plain text editor, and never in a Word-type document editor that corrupts the formatting.
Stop posting any claim that fails the balance check, and record the result of the investigation.
Map every denial and recovery back to the original billing month before calculating any denial rate.
Require a dollar outcome, a payback month, and a named human reviewer for every automation or vendor proposal.

fields.name: group_code_triage
fields.prompt: Pull your last ten remittances and sort every adjustment by group code. Record which CO lines are true contractual write-offs, which PR lines the patient may owe, and which CARCs require action instead of routine posting.
fields.example: Of 212 adjustment lines, 168 were CO45 contractual write-offs, 31 were PR1 deductible amounts moved to patient statements, and 13 carried 16, 29, or 197 and went to the action queue. Confusing CO with PR is how patients end up billed for write-offs [Health Weave RCM LLC — bPFE9F4Y_Y4 @ 00:03:18], so a second reviewer checks every PR line.

fields.name: claim_balance_check
fields.prompt: Run the balance check on one claim from your newest 835: charged minus contractual adjustment equals allowed, and paid plus patient share equals allowed. Show every number, and state what you did when the math did not balance.
fields.example: Claim billed $200; CO45 adjustment $80 leaves $120 allowed; PR1 deductible $100 plus $20 paid equals $120, so the line balances [Health Weave RCM LLC — bPFE9F4Y_Y4 @ 00:05:52]. A second claim missed by $14, so posting stopped and we investigated before touching the account, as the balance rule requires [Michael Roberts — HolIPG8-TV8 @ 00:01:39].

fields.name: zero_paid_line_review
fields.prompt: List every zero-paid line in the current posting batch and classify each as a true denial or a deductible application. For each, record the allowed amount, the deductible column, the group code, and where the balance was routed.
fields.example: Nine zero-paid lines this batch. Seven showed the allowed amount equal to the deductible column with PR1, so they posted to the patient rather than the denial queue [Inlera University — -zx82Gn2h04 @ 00:04:18]. Two were true denials with CARC 16 and went to correction. Secondary coverage was checked before any patient statement went out.

fields.name: deposit_reconciliation
fields.prompt: Describe how each batch is reconciled to the bank: matching the TRN trace number to the EFT, matching deposit totals to remittance totals, working PLB recoupment lines, and handling any EFT that arrived without a remittance.
fields.example: The TRN on Tuesday's 835 matched the EFT, but the deposit ran $312 short of the remittance total; a PLB recoupment line explained the gap and was worked before closing [Health Weave RCM LLC — bPFE9F4Y_Y4 @ 00:09:19]. One EFT arrived with no remittance, so we pulled the portal PDF before posting [The Claim Game X Practice Solutions — FE6Ns41GFH0 @ 00:11:04].

fields.name: contract_underpayment_audit
fields.prompt: Match a sample of remittances against your loaded fee schedules and contracts. Record the allowed amount each payer used, the contracted amount, the per-claim variance, the annual volume, and the projected dollar gap if the variance continues.
fields.example: Allowed amounts on one payer ran 75 cents to $1 below contract on every claim [The Claim Game X Practice Solutions — FE6Ns41GFH0 @ 00:13:50]. Across 40,000 annual claims that gap reaches up to $40,000. A similar 60-day remittance audit cut accounts receivable 30 to 40 percent [The Claim Game X Practice Solutions — FE6Ns41GFH0 @ 00:15:33], so posting now includes a contract check.

fields.name: recurring_reason_code_root_cause
fields.prompt: Identify the three reason codes that recur most across your remittances this quarter. For each, trace the upstream cause, name the fix applied at the source, and record whether the code dropped after the fix instead of being resubmitted repeatedly.
fields.example: CARC 197 led the list. Before rewriting codes, the auth field was checked: 70553 approved and 70551 billed was supported by the crosswalk, and the real error was a case number in the authorization field [RCM Pulse Academy — Ut5VjfFul68 @ 00:12:34]. Fixing the field template cut repeats, since the fix belongs upstream [Health Weave RCM LLC — bPFE9F4Y_Y4 @ 00:09:51].

fields.name: matched_denial_rate
fields.prompt: Calculate your matched denial rate by mapping denials and recoveries back to the original billing month. Record the gross denial percentage, the recovered percentage, the resulting net denial rate, and the payer contributing the largest share.
fields.example: Mapped to the June billing month, 15 percent of claims denied and 7 percent were recovered, exposing the true net denial rate [Practical Data Solutions - Healthcare Analytics — 4SW5Ihdk8ps @ 00:20:29]. Eligibility drove the largest share, consistent with 24 percent of denials coming from eligibility against a 12 percent industry denial rate [OpenBots — ZpELLvKSrF8 @ 00:00:25].

fields.name: automation_readiness_case
fields.prompt: Build the financial case for your first automation project. Record the starting workflow, data cleanliness issues such as coordination of benefits, cost per manual check, cost per reworked denial, expected payback month, and the human review step that remains.
fields.example: Starting point is eligibility, the easiest to automate and hardest to ignore [OpenBots — ZpELLvKSrF8 @ 00:25:41]. Coordination of benefits drives about half of eligibility errors, so COB data gets cleaned first [OpenBots — ZpELLvKSrF8 @ 00:14:02]. The model prices $5 per manual check and $118 per reworked denial, with payback expected by month 3 to 4. Humans still sign exceptions.

fields.name: vendor_contract_controls
fields.prompt: List the controls you will write into any AI or RCM vendor contract: required KPIs, reporting feedback loops, appeal timeframes, specialty-matched medical necessity review, and the test you will use to detect repackaged RPA sold as AI.
fields.example: The draft contract names denial rate and appeal turnaround as KPIs with a monthly feedback report, and screens claimed AI for repackaged RPA, because a vendor relationship should not be an annuity [HealthLeaders Media — BKBNIfZ081U @ 01:00:19]. Payer contracts now require same-specialty medical necessity review, since we get the behavior we tolerate [HealthLeaders Media — BKBNIfZ081U @ 00:10:32].

fields.name: idr_volume_and_hold_discipline
fields.prompt: Describe how back-end automation will handle IDR submission volume and held claims. Record the expected award multiple of QPA, the win rate assumed, the internal release clock, and the rule that stops staff from releasing held claims under deadline pressure.
fields.example: Modeling assumes awards at 2 to 3 times QPA and a 75 percent win rate, the range reported by a team handling 200,000 IDR submissions a month [HealthLeaders Media — BKBNIfZ081U @ 00:55:37]. Held claims are never released because a deadline feels close; the internal 4 p.m. clock stays separate from the payer clock [RCM Pulse Academy — Ut5VjfFul68 @ 00:18:57].

worksheets.completion_gate: Part 2 is complete only when every batch reconciles to its deposit, every PLB line is worked, every zero-paid line is classified, the top three recurring codes have upstream fixes, and every automation or vendor proposal carries KPIs, a payback month, and a named human review step.
